title: The Economy Grows, but Americans Feel Worse About It

source.author: Jim Tyson
source.title: Economic optimism plunges to lowest level since Great Recession
source.checked_against: Single source: a news report of surveys by Gallup, Harris, the University of Michigan, the Commerce Department and NABE. Figures come only from this article; the original surveys were not opened. The link to the November 3 elections, the motor vehicle figure, the quotes from Pantheon about tax refunds and energy prices, the 3% wage figure, last month's 2.1% growth forecast, and the Group of Seven remark are left out. 'Optimistic' is written as 'positive', 'recession' as 'a serious fall in the economy', and 'economists' as 'business experts' to stay inside the reader's vocabulary.

figures.text: share of U.S. adults optimistic about the economy fell from 47% last year to 29% this year; lowest since Gallup began the poll in 2007
figures.quote: slumped from 47% last year to 29% this year, hitting the lowest level since Gallup launched a poll of the public view toward the economy in 2007

figures.text: lowest level since the 2007 to 2009 Great Recession; wage gains failed to keep pace with inflation
figures.quote: the lowest level since the 2007 to 2009 Great Recession as wage gains failed to keep pace with persistent inflation, Gallup said

figures.text: last time the mood dropped this sharply was the financial crash of the Great Recession
figures.quote: The last time that economic sentiment dropped this sharply was during the financial crash

figures.text: no matching drop in GDP now
figures.quote: However, there has been no corresponding drop in GDP to match the worsening public mood.

figures.text: Harris poll (reported by The Guardian): three out of four Americans concerned about a recession last month; 61% wrongly believe a downturn has already started
figures.quote: Three out of four Americans last month said they are concerned about a recession and 61% incorrectly believe the U.S. is already suffering a downturn

figures.text: University of Michigan: consumer sentiment up 6% this month from October, still 10% below February
figures.quote: Although consumer sentiment rose 6% this month compared with October, it is still 10% below the February level, the University of Michigan said.

figures.text: about 57% say high prices have eroded their living standards (Joanne Hsu, director of consumer surveys)
figures.quote: roughly 57% of respondents saying spontaneously that high prices have eroded their living standards, Joanne Hsu, the university’s director of consumer surveys, said

figures.text: Commerce Department: retail sales up 0.2% in October month over month, slowing from 0.8% in September
figures.quote: Retail sales month over month increased 0.2% in October, slowing from 0.8% in September.

figures.text: furniture and home furnishing store spending fell 2.3% after gaining 3.6% in September
figures.quote: Spending at furniture and home furnishing stores fell 2.3% after gaining 3.6% in September

figures.text: Olivia Cross, senior U.S. economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics: the negative trend will likely accelerate; consumption strength expected to wane this quarter
figures.quote: The negative trend will likely accelerate, Olivia Cross, senior U.S. economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics, said Tuesday.

figures.text: Q3 economy expanded more than forecast, largely because of investment in artificial intelligence
figures.quote: the economy during Q3 expanded more than forecast, in large part because of robust investment in the building blocks for artificial intelligence

figures.text: NABE survey median forecast: economy to grow 2.4% this year
figures.quote: The economy this year will likely grow 2.4%, according to the median forecast in a survey by the National Association for Business Economics.

figures.text: more than half of NABE panelists do not expect the next recession to begin before 2029
figures.quote: more than half of panelists do not expect the next recession to begin before 2029

figures.text: Gallup: perception of the economy increasingly detached from GDP since 2022, after the inflation spike and slower wage growth
figures.quote: become increasingly detached from GDP since 2022, following the spike in inflation and the slowdown in wage growth
